question: T12 (task-6d696bed02adf319): on the desktop, a one-step fall of Wave Intensity (180 to 150) on a Scrolling block made 1/2/12/26 by hand (CAP-T12HANDFALL: the foot goes from 12 to 11), with a Text block that starts between the new and the old foot: on row 11 (the new foot) or row 12 (the old foot). Does it stay or follow the foot up? On Blocks Probe at a 1600 by 1000 window, one new section per plan with a new Scrolling block and a Text block added after it (desktop 1/2/3/26 and 1/2/3/10). Then 'open' (select the Scrolling block, Edit, Design), a press on Wave Intensity at the range's end (180: 1/2/7/26), 'go' (Escape and a press on the page); 'place i r0/c0/r1/c1' moves and resizes block i by hand: the Scrolling block to 1/2/12/26 (11 rows, its line needs 6), and the Text block to 11/2/13/10 (C1) or 12/2/14/10 (C2). Then 'open', a press on 150, 'go', and Cmd+Z until as built. R1 and R2 are two sessions (R1a, R2a, probe-z.mjs), each with plans of other tasks. Exit without saving each time.
readsAre: As CAP-T12DRAGFALL: layout of the Scrolling block and every block in its section (me: the Scrolling block; line: its drawing's height; sel: selected; kind; desktop and phone areas, top in the section and height), the section rows in the view shown, the Scrolling block's height, line (marquee and svg: top in the block and height), Undo and Redo, the panel's ranges; 'wave' is the panel's Wave Intensity value. 'inputs' holds each drag's quick reads (states: [name, { t: the page's clock, L: the layout as in reads, st: value, focus (isRange: the range has it), Undo/Redo, selected blocks, lines }]) and its events by the page's clock from the first (log: type, ms, the range's value). The read's name is the run, the plan, and the steps in order, '>' between them ('Z' is Cmd+Z, skipped when the section is back as built).
answer: C1 and C2 alike for the Scrolling block: 150 takes it from 1/2/12/26 to 1/2/11/26 (one row, CAP-T12HANDFALL's rule).
C1: the Text block at 11/2/13/10 starts on the new foot (11) and stays; the section keeps 12 rows.

C2: the Text block at 12/2/14/10 starts on the old foot (12), under the new one, and goes up by the foot's fall to 11/2/13/10; the section goes from 13 rows to 12. So the desktop fall rule holds here too: a block that starts on or above the new foot stays, one under it follows the foot up.

The press is one undo step: the first Cmd+Z gives back 1/2/12/26 with the Text block where it was placed (and the section's 13 rows in C2); the next one takes back the place. R1 and R2 read alike in every read (areas, rows, line, Undo and Redo).
Not read: a Text block that starts on row 11 and ends above the old foot, a drag or keys through the step, other window widths, the phone view.
